Nevertheless, we show that introducing locus-specific boundaries into CLCs can produce simulated Hi-C contact maps with topologically associating domains (TADs), which are observed experimentally for these species. Finally, by mapping RNA-seq data onto our simulated conformations, we find no enrichment of transcriptional activity at the chromosome periphery. Our results challenge the long-standing CLC model and suggest that dinoflagellate chromosomes are organized into condensed structures with local but not global order that does not impede transcription.

title: Targeted degradation of P-TEFb via MDM2 substrate substitution collapses oncogenic transcriptional programs in MDM2-amplified cancers.
abstract: MDM2 is an oncogenic E3 ubiquitin ligase best known for targeting the tumor suppressor p53 and is frequently amplified in human cancers, including dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS). We show that supraphysiological MDM2 expression can be exploited to reprogram its ligase activity toward selective degradation of oncogenic transcriptional machinery. Using a substrate substitution strategy, we developed an MDM2-recruiting degrader dCDK9-010 that targets positive transcription elongation factor b, inducing its proteasomal degradation while simultaneously stabilizing p53. This dual action disrupts RNA polymerase II abundance and elongation, preferentially impairing enhancer-driven transcriptional programs that sustain tumor growth. In DDLPS models, this approach produces potent antitumor activity with favorable pharmacokinetic and safety profiles, triggers apoptosis, and enhances macrophage-mediated tumor cell clearance. These findings establish substrate substitution-based reprogramming of MDM2 as a generalizable targeted protein degradation strategy and identify MDM2 amplification as a predictive biomarker for therapeutic response across cancer types, with particular relevance to liposarcoma.

title: Distinct Thermosensitive Activation of HSF1 and HSF2 in Immune Cells During Aging.
abstract: Heat shock factors (HSF1 and HSF2) critically maintain proteostasis under stress, yet their activation across the continuum of rising temperatures is incompletely understood. Furthermore, how age impacts thermally driven rheostatic changes in stress responses is not fully elucidated. Here, we investigate how different temperature levels impact HSF1 and HSF2 in Jurkat T cells and splenocytes from young and aged mice. Using Western blotting, EMSA, RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence, and co-immunoprecipitation, we examined heat shock response changes across a range of thermal conditions. Unlike most cell types that require 42°C for HSF1 activation, Jurkat cells maximally responded at 41°C and splenocytes at 40°C. Optimal HSF1 activation coincided with maximal nuclear translocation, Ser326 phosphorylation, SIRT1 protein levels, and HSP RNA levels. By contrast, HSF2 nuclear translocation required a higher temperature (42°C) than HSF1. Age reduced HSF1 protein levels and nuclear translocation during thermal stress, while HSF2 protein levels were significantly elevated. These findings reveal distinct temperature-sensitive patterns of HSF1 and HSF2 activation of immunocytes during heat stress and identify age-associated alterations in this response.

title: Joint representation of spliced and unspliced RNA expands information content in single-cell expression data.
abstract: Single-cell RNA-seq captures both mature (spliced) and nascent (unspliced) transcripts, yet standard preprocessing collapses these signals into a single expression matrix, obscuring recoverable structure and introducing splicing-dependent artifacts in downstream analysis. We asked whether treating spliced and unspliced counts as distinct feature sets increases recoverable latent structure in unsupervised dimension reduction. Across four datasets, we applied non-negative matrix factorization to spliced-only, unspliced-only, added, and concatenated representations, estimating the revealable rank, the largest stable rank achieving near-optimal held-out error, by cross-validation. Concatenated representations exceeded the added representation in all four datasets and surpassed both single-modality inputs in three of four, indicating that preserving splicing status exposes additional stable latent programs beyond either modality alone or their sum. Minimal overlap between spliced- and unspliced-derived factors corresponded to modality-specific gene set enrichment consistent with complementary steady-state and nascent regulatory activity. These results establish splicing status as an informative axis of variation and motivate preserving spliced and unspliced layers as first-class features to maximize information recovery. The singlet R package is available at github.com/zdebruine/singlet. Code to reproduce all figures is available at github.com/Arya-86/nmf-spliced-unspliced.

title: Single-cell dissection of shoulder-derived mesenchymal stem cells reveals source-specific progenitor heterogeneity and a SIX2-driven chondrogenic program.
abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) within the shoulder joint serve as a critical progenitor pool for regenerating the fibrocartilaginous enthesis during rotator cuff repair. However, the chondrogenic potential of MSCs across distinct rotator cuff sites, along with the underlying molecular mechanisms, remains to be elucidated. We performed a comparative analysis of human subacromial bursa-derived MSCs (sMSCs) and rotator cuff enthesis-derived MSCs (rMSCs). By integrating functional chondrogenic assays with longitudinal bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, we reconstructed source-specific differentiation trajectories and identified key regulatory drivers. rMSCs exhibited superior chondrogenic potency compared to sMSCs. Transcriptional profiling identified a region-specific pro-chondrogenic module in rMSCs driven by the transcription factor SIX2. Single-cell atlas construction revealed that tissue origin dictates lineage fate: rMSCs were enriched for a high-potency SIX2+ progenitor population that differentiated into metabolic-active S100A2+ chondrocytes. Conversely, sMSCs were dominated by DPP4+ progenitors that preferentially bifurcated into an aberrant CXCL8+ inflammatory trajectory. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that SIX2 acted as a competency factor, coordinating early proliferative expansion with late-stage matrix assembly and, crucially, active suppression of inflammatory signaling. Accordingly, lentiviral overexpression of SIX2 in sMSCs was sufficient to rescue their chondrogenic defects and rewire their trajectory toward a regenerative phenotype. Our findings define the transcriptional hierarchy of shoulder-resident progenitors, identifying SIX2 as a master regulator that couples chondrogenesis with immune evasion. This establishes a molecular framework for precision cell sourcing and rational design of lineage-specific therapies.

title: Endothelial regulators in the infrapatellar fat pad of osteoarthritis revealed by integrative multi-omics and genetic causal inference.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a multifactorial degenerative joint disease involving multiple joint components, including the infrapatellar fat pad (IFP), whose role in OA pathogenesis remains poorly understood. In this study, we employed an integrative multi-omics strategy to delineate the cellular and molecular landscape of the IFP in OA. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data, we identified endothelial cells as key mediators within the IFP microenvironment, exhibiting strong intercellular communication. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from endothelial cells were subjected to Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis, integrating expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL), protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL), and genome-wide association study (GWAS) datasets. This analysis revealed family with sequence similarity 241 member A (FAM241A) and thymidine kinase 2 (TK2) as endothelial-specific causal regulators of OA, with FAM241A associated with a protective effect and TK2 with increased disease risk. Pathway analyses suggested distinct biological roles for FAM241A and TK2. Both genes demonstrated progressively increased expression along pseudotime trajectories. Spatial transcriptomics (ST) revealed region-specific expression patterns, further supporting their involvement in IFP remodeling. Collectively, this study identifies FAM241A and TK2 as novel endothelial-specific causal genes in the IFP of OA, and uncovers temporally and spatially regulated transcriptional programs. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into OA pathogenesis and propose promising targets for biomarker development and therapeutic intervention.

title: Aromaticity at spike position 456 affects functional immunogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant receptor-binding domain.
abstract: The recurrent emergence of the F456L substitution in SARS-CoV-2 Omicron sublineages has been associated with immune evasion, yet its impact on vaccine-induced immune responses remains poorly understood. Using a trimeric RBD-HR subunit vaccine platform, we investigated how residue 456 influences the functional immunogenicity of the receptor-binding domain (RBD). We found that the F456L substitution markedly reduced neutralizing antibody responses against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, despite maintaining comparable levels of total antigen-specific IgG, indicating a selective impairment of functional immunogenicity rather than overall antigenicity. Single-cell RNA sequencing and B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire analyses further revealed that the F456L mutation weakened germinal center responses, reduced clonal expansion, and impaired repertoire remodeling of antigen-specific B cells. Structural modeling, biolayer interferometry, and calcium flux assays demonstrated that aromatic residues at position 456 promote effective germline BCR recognition and activation. Importantly, replacing the non-aromatic leucine residue with aromatic amino acids, including tyrosine or tryptophan, restored the neutralizing antibody-eliciting capacity of the antigen. Together, these findings identify aromaticity at residue 456 as a critical determinant of RBD functional immunogenicity and demonstrate how a single amino acid substitution can reshape B-cell responses and antibody quality. This work provides important insights for rational vaccine antigen design and advances our understanding of how site-specific mutations regulate antiviral immunity.

title: Regulatory mechanism of M2d tumor-associated macrophage-derived exosomal apolipoprotein E on platinum resistance in ovarian cancer.
abstract: Platinum-based chemotherapy plus cytoreductive surgery represents the standard first-line therapy for ovarian cancer (OC), which yields robust early therapeutic responses in most patients. However, platinum resistance is a formidable clinical hurdle, and how macrophages mediate drug resistance within the OC tumor microenvironment remains poorly understood. We cultured SKOV3 OC cells and THP-1 monocytes, induced THP-1 differentiation into M2d tumor-associated macrophages. Stable apolipoprotein E (ApoE) -overexpressing SKOV3 cell lines were constructed via lentiviral transfection and puromycin screening. We established nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft models with mixed tumor cells and M2d macrophages, administered cisplatin treatment and collected tumor tissues after sacrifice by cervical dislocation. RNA was extracted from tumor samples to conduct RT-qPCR for gene expression detection. Tumor tissue sections were prepared for HE staining, TUNEL apoptosis staining, and Western blot analysis to detect ApoE and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/AKT/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway protein expression. Using nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft models, we demonstrated that M2d-type tumor-associated macrophages (M2d TAMs) promote platinum resistance and elevate tumoral ApoE levels. In OC xenografts with stable ApoE overexpression, cisplatin-induced apoptosis was profoundly repressed, resulting in reduced cisplatin sensitivity, while this inhibitory effect was not observed in the empty vector control group. Mechanistically, ApoE activates the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling cascade to counteract cisplatin cytotoxicity by suppressing cell death and sustaining pro-survival signals. Overall, this study reveals that M2d TAMs induce platinum resistance in OC cells via exosomes carrying ApoE.

title: Caveolin-1-Mediated Tight Junction Assembly and Intestinal Permeability in Necrotizing Enterocolitis.
abstract: Introduction: Necrotizing Enterocolitis (NEC) is a gastrointestinal emergency in premature neonates. Its multifactorial pathogenesis includes increased permeability and dysregulated inflammation. Caveolin-1 regulates intestinal permeability via endocytosis and trafficking of tight junction proteins, specifically occludin. We hypothesize that caveolin-1 expression is altered in NEC leading to decreased tight junction protein trafficking and increased intestinal permeability. Methods: Wild-type and caveolin-1 knockout mice underwent experimental NEC for survival analysis followed by tissue harvest for histologic evaluation, permeability assay, RNA and protein extraction, immunohistochemistry, and enteroid generation. Enteroids derived from wild-type and caveolin-1 knockout mice underwent experimental NEC followed by permeability assay and RNA extraction for RT-qPCR. Additionally, tissue from human patients with and without active NEC underwent protein extraction for western blot and immunofluorescent staining. Results: Caveolin-1 knockout mice had worsened experimental NEC on gross and histologic analysis compared to wild-type and decreased survival (p<0.05,p=0.003). Caveolin-1 knockout enteroids had increased permeability following experimental NEC (p=0.022, p=0.006). Occludin localization was more disorganized and expression was decreased in experimental caveolin-1 knockout mice compared to wild-type (p=0.002). Caveolin-1 and occludin protein was found to be decreased in active human NEC tissue compared to control (p=0.004, p=0.025). Conclusion: Caveolin-1 deficiency is associated with decreased survival and more severe histologic disease in a mouse model of NEC. Caveolin-1 expression is decreased in NEC, which correlates with a decrease in occludin expression and resultant increase in intestinal permeability. Our work suggests caveolin-1 deficiency may lead to a predisposition to increased permeability in response to NEC.

title: Grain-sized moxibustion attenuates renal dysfunction and inflammation in naturally aging micethe phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B/nuclear factor-κB pathway.
abstract: To investigate the potential mechanisms by which Zusanli (ST36) moxibustion alleviates age-related renal lesions viaregulating inflammation. Male mice were divided into three groups: the young group (adult mice aged 3 months), the old group (21-month-old mice maintained until 24 months), and the grain-sized moxibustion (GS-Moxi) group [21-month-old mice treated with grain-sized moxibustion (GS-Moxi) at Zusanli (ST36) for 3 months]. To assess the protective effects of GS-Moxi on age-related renal injury, serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen levels, and renal tissue were analyzed using periodic acid-Schiff and Masson's trichrome staining. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) was conducted for gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and kyoto encyclopedia of genes and genomes (KEGG) pathway analysis. Additionally, Western blotting and immunohistochemistry (IHC) were employed to examine the involvement of the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/ protein kinase B/nuclear factor-κB (PI3K/AKT/NF-κB) signaling pathway in response to GS-Moxi treatment. Our findings demonstrated that GS-Moxi significantly improved renal histopathological features and ameliorated age-related renal dysfunction. Additionally, GS-Moxi attenuated the upregulation of fibrosis markers, senescence markers [p16, p21, and senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal)], oxidative stress markers (superoxide dismutase (SOD) and malondialdehyde (MDA)), and inflammatory cytokines [tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-1β (IL-1β)] in the aging kidneys. Transcriptomic analysis, followed by GSEA and KEGG pathway enrichment, revealed the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway as a critical regulatory pathway. Western blotting and IHC further confirmed that GS-Moxi modulates the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathway in the aging kidney. Our study confirmed that GS-Moxi at ST36 has a significant therapeutic effect on age-related renal injury by inhibiting the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathway, thereby reducing the release of inflammatory factors and mitigating oxidative stress injury.

title: Caffeic acid mitigates myocardial fibrosis via suppressing MAPKs/CREB-mediated inflammation in myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury mice.
abstract: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) represents a major form of secondary damage during reperfusion therapy, in which inflammation and myocardial fibrosis are key pathological features. Caffeic acid (CA), a natural phenolic compound abundant in dietary sources, has been implicated in cardiovascular protection; however, the mechanisms by which CA modulates post-MIRI inflammation and fibrosis remain insufficiently defined. To clarify the molecular target(s) and signaling mechanism(s) through which CA attenuates inflammation-associated myocardial fibrosis after MIRI. A LAD ligation-based murine MIRI model was used to evaluate the anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic efficacy of CA. A co-culture system using cardiac fibroblasts and RAW 264.7 macrophages, along with adoptive cell transfer, was applied to interrogate macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk. Transcriptomic profiling (RNA-seq) was performed to identify candidate pathways involved in CA-mediated protection. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay, CETSA, immunofluorescence, and western blotting were used to assess MAPKs/CREB signaling as a putative intervention axis, and pharmacological activation of MAPKs (anisomycin) or CREB (forskolin), or MAPK14 ablation, was employed to probe pathway involvement. CA improved cardiac function and alleviated inflammatory and fibrotic pathology in MIRI mice, accompanied by suppression of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Conditioned medium from LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 cells promoted fibroblast activation, and adoptively transferred macrophages within the myocardium promoted fibrotic protein expression; both effects were attenuated by CA. RNA-seq implicated MAPK signaling in the protective mechanism of CA, and downstream analyses supported inhibition of the MAPKs/CREB axis. Notably, CA achieved effects comparable to those of MAPK14 ablation, whereas anisomycin or forskolin partially blunted the anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic effects of CA, consistent with functional involvement of MAPKs/CREB signaling in CA-mediated protection during MIRI. CA mitigates MIRI-associated myocardial fibrosis by suppressing MAPKs/CREB-mediated inflammatory signaling, supporting its potential to improve long-term post-MIRI remodeling.

title: Neoantigen nanovaccines for cancer immunotherapy: design strategies, translational bottlenecks, and clinical prospects.
abstract: Neoantigen vaccines have become an important direction in cancer immunotherapy because mutation-derived tumor antigens can induce highly specific T-cell responses while minimizing immune tolerance associated with tumor-associated antigens. However, their therapeutic performance remains limited by several delivery-related barriers, including rapid antigen degradation, insufficient lymphatic trafficking, weak dendritic-cell activation, and inefficient cross-presentation. Nanotechnology provides flexible strategies to overcome these limitations. This review first summarizes the major delivery mechanisms by which nanocarriers enhance neoantigen presentation and T-cell priming, followed by recent preclinical and clinical advances in neoantigen nanovaccine platforms. Beyond these advances, we highlight the heterogeneity of clinical outcomes across different vaccine platforms and emphasize that vaccine-induced immunogenicity does not always translate into objective clinical benefit. We then analyze major translational bottlenecks, including prolonged neoantigen identification, tumor heterogeneity and neoantigen loss, formulation variability, manufacturing scalability, quality control, and tumor microenvironment-mediated immune resistance. Emerging strategies, including artificial intelligence-assisted neoantigen prioritization, broad-spectrum antigen induction, immunogenicity enhancement, RNA and nanocarrier platform optimization, rational combination therapy, clinically relevant model validation, and biomarker-driven patient stratification, are further discussed. Finally, we propose that future development should integrate rational nanocarrier design with patient stratification, tumor microenvironment modulation, large-scale multicenter clinical validation, standardized manufacturing, and robust potency evaluation. This review aims to provide a translational perspective for the rational development of next-generation neoantigen nanovaccines with improved efficacy, safety, and clinical feasibility.

title: Transcriptional and functional profiling reveals a dynamic continuum of beta-cell activation states.
abstract: A central question is whether beta-cells respond uniformly to glucose. Using phospho-S6 as an activation marker, this study shows that beta-cells are recruited sequentially as glucose concentrations increase. Recruitment is spatially organized, with high-threshold cells predominantly located in the islet core. Transcriptomic profiling indicates functional heterogeneity among beta-cells. A low-threshold subset is characterized by enhanced stress resilience necessary for sustained secretion. An intermediate subset, enriched for calcium-signaling and vesicle-excitatory genes, modulates postprandial glucose excursions. The high-threshold subset specializes in high-capacity protein synthesis and insulin secretion to manage glucose peaks. Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals that these functional subsets form a continuous spectrum rather than discrete subpopulations. This division of labor is adaptable; under high-fat diet-induced metabolic demand, islets undergo remodeling with a global reduction in activation thresholds and a shift toward high-capacity profiles. Collectively, these findings identify a beta-cell hierarchy that balances metabolic resilience with secretory demand to maintain glucose homeostasis.

title: Th2 cell-mediated ferroptosis as a driver of sebaceous gland dysfunction in atopic dermatitis.
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease accompanied by reduced sebum production and skin dryness, yet the functional states of the sebaceous gland (SG, a key tissue for sebum production) in the pathogenesis of AD remain unclear. We fully explored the number, morphology, and function of SG in AD through multiomics, animal intervention experiments, and mechanistic studies. Integrated high-resolution and spot-level spatial transcriptomics, single-cell/bulk RNA sequencing, metabolomics, and histological analysis revealed a marked reduction in SG number in AD, accompanied by morphological atrophy and impaired lipid metabolism, which was closely associated with elevated ferroptosis levels in SG. Topical application of the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) significantly ameliorated AD-like dermatitis in MC903-treated mice, restoring SG morphology and function, while reducing Th2 cell infiltration and lowering transepidermal water loss (TEWL). Spatial transcriptomic mapping and immunofluorescence localization demonstrated Th2 cells exhibited the strongest spatial proximity to SG in AD lesional skin, indicating the effect of Th2 cells on ferroptosis in SG. Further communication profiling indicated that Th2-derived IL-4 may target GPX4 in SG. In vitro, treatment of SG cells (SZ95) with IL-4 increased ferroptosis levels and decreased GPX4 protein expression. Mechanistically, IL-4 enhanced the binding between TRIM15 and GPX4, which mediated the K48-linked ubiquitination and degradation of GPX4. Consistently, blockade of IL-4 or IL-4Rα using an anti-IL-4 antibody or dupilumab effectively alleviated SG ferroptosis, reduced TEWL, and attenuated the severity of AD-like dermatitis. Our study reveals a mechanistic link between Th2 inflammation and SG ferroptosis via IL-4-TRIM15-GPX4-ubiquitination signaling, thus offering new insights into SG dysfunction and skin barrier impairment in AD. CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Reduced sebum production and skin dryness are notable clinical manifestations of atopic dermatitis (AD). Our study revealed that ferroptosis of the sebaceous gland (SG) may disrupt sebum production in AD, thus offering new insight into AD therapy by highlighting sebum homeostasis as a potential therapeutic target. Sebaceous gland (SG) ferroptosis, which contributes to reduced sebum production and skin barrier dysfunction in atopic dermatitis (AD), is driven by Th2 cell-derived IL-4 via TRIM15/GPX4 ubiquitination.

title: Decoding proteomic complexity of transcript variants and homologous isoforms for precision therapeutics.
abstract: The traditional "one gene, one protein" paradigm is insufficient to capture the vast phenotypic and physiological complexity of eukaryotes. This review aims to comprehensively elucidate the molecular mechanisms of transcriptomic diversification, namely, alternative splicing, alternative usage of promoter, and alternative polyadenylation, and their profound impacts on cellular homeostasis and human disease. By synthesizing recent breakthroughs in targeted long-read RNA sequencing, single-cell isoform-specific multiomics, and AI-driven 3D structural modeling, we systematically examine how transcript variants are generated and functionally annotated. Our analysis highlights that multiple transcript variants originating from a single genetic locus are not merely redundant copies; rather, subtle sequence alterations dynamically rewire protein-protein interaction networks and dictate precise subcellular localization. The exquisite spatiotemporal regulation of these variants controls critical cell fate decisions and organ development. Consequently, the pathological dysregulation of these processes, frequently termed spliceopathies, acts as a primary driver in severe pathologies, including cancer multidrug resistance, metabolic reprogramming, and neurodegenerative disorders. In conclusion, understanding the eukaryotic proteome requires a fundamental shift from conventional gene-level to isoform-level perspectives. Decoding the complex regulatory syntax of transcript variants paves the way for next-generation precision medicine, highlighting the therapeutic potential of RNA-targeted interventions, such as antisense oligonucleotides and CRISPR-based RNA editing, to correct pathogenic isoforms.

title: PROMISE-Surv: Proteomics-guided survival representation transfer for deployable transcriptomic cancer modeling.
abstract: Deep proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiling captures functional tumor signaling, but these assays are unavailable in most large survival cohorts. Existing multi-omics approaches often require complete molecular profiles or reconstruction of missing modalities, leaving unclear whether survival-relevant protein-layer information can be transferred directly to routinely available data. We therefore investigated whether proteomics-informed survival structure could be transferred to an RNA-plus-clinical model without reconstructing missing protein measurements. PROMISE-Surv was developed as a teacher-student framework using complete-case CPTAC/PDC tumors from lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC), and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSC) as the multimodal discovery cohort (n = 314). The student model was then deployed in matched TCGA cohorts from the same cancer types (n = 1571), with independent GEO cohorts used as endpoint-specific external stress tests. Across ten repeated held-out splits, the blended student achieved a mean C-index of 0.687 (95% CI, 0.638-0.730); matched discovery scores preserved teacher-derived risk ordering across all three cancers (Spearman ρ=0.981-0.989). In TCGA, transferred risk stratified survival in KIRC and LUAD and recovered cancer-specific RNA programs linked to adverse tumor biology, with concordant pathway-level support from RPPA. Cross-cancer analysis identified eight directionally conserved RNA-risk markers, while enrichment of the broader candidate ranking implicated RNA processing and ribosome biogenesis. These findings support biological coherence of the transferred risk representation. PROMISE-Surv provides a biological-transfer framework for extending proteomics-informed survival structure to RNA-plus-clinical cohorts without protein-layer measurements.

title: Machine-learning-assisted integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics characterizes glioblastoma ecosystem states and immune-associated programs.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by marked malignant-cell plasticity and a complex tumor ecosystem composed of heterogeneous malignant and microenvironmental cell populations. We integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to characterize reproducible GBM cell and ecosystem-associated states, evaluate cross-platform concordance, and examine immune-associated transcriptional programs while distinguishing descriptive associations from mechanistic inference. The deposited Smart-seq2 (7,930 cells) and 10x (16,201 cells) expression matrices from GSE131928/SCP393 were analyzed on their verified expression scales. Official annotations and malignant-state modules were audited, four broad malignant states were recomputed, and a tumor-held-out machine-learning label-transfer framework was applied to the 10x dataset. Public TCGA-GBM RNA-seq data were used to evaluate state- and microenvironment-associated transcriptional programs and to perform nested prediction benchmarking. Selected ecosystem-associated genes were additionally examined by RT-qPCR in glioma cell lines and normal human astrocytes. Among Smart-seq2 cells, 6,576 malignant cells had valid state scores, whereas 287 alias-affected records were excluded from state-score denominators. The machine-learning label-transfer model achieved an out-of-fold accuracy of 0.998, and malignant-state fractions showed moderate-to-strong concordance across six shared tumor labels. At the tumor-label level, MES-like fraction was not significantly associated with macrophage fraction (Spearman rho = 0.171, P = 0.395), indicating that ecosystem-level transcriptional association should not be interpreted as a simple directional immune-to-state mechanism. In TCGA-GBM, MES and myeloid-associated programs correlated with immune and stromal expression signatures, whereas survival and 12-month prediction performance remained modest and specification-sensitive. RT-qPCR further demonstrated increased STAT3, CHI3L1, SPP1, and VEGFA expression in glioma cell lines relative to normal human astrocytes. Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis supports reproducible characterization of malignant-cell heterogeneity and immune-associated ecosystem features in IDH-wildtype GBM. Machine-learning-assisted cross-platform analysis provides a reproducible framework for evaluating tumor ecosystem-associated states, while the observed immune-mesenchymal associations remain descriptive rather than causal. Experimental RT-qPCR provides expression-level support for selected ecosystem-associated genes and highlights testable hypotheses for future functional and spatial studies.

title: Non-electrophilic TRPA1 modulator MNP-021 protects neuronal and glial function from diabetes-associated glucotoxicity and neuroinflammation.
abstract: Diabetes-associated neurodegeneration is amplified by methylglyoxal (MGO)-driven dicarbonyl stress linking hyperglycemia to neuronal insulin resistance and maladaptive neuroinflammation. We tested the neuroprotective activity of MNP-021, a non-electrophilic transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) modulator, in neurons and glial cells in vitro. SH-SY5Y neurons were pretreated with MNP-021 and challenged with MGO, then profiled by high-content imaging, RNA-seq, Seahorse Oxygen Consumption Rate (OCR) and Extracellular Acidification Rate (ECAR), glycolytic stress assays, and immunoblotting for AKT, ERK, and cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB). In an additional sustained glucotoxicity paradigm, differentiated SH-SY5Y cells were exposed to high glucose for 7 days and viability was assessed by LIVE/DEAD™ high-content imaging. HMC3 glial cells were treated with MNP-021, exposed to Lipopolysaccharide (LPS), Tumor Necrosis Factor-α (TNF-α) or Aβ(25-35), and tested for viability and inflammatory markers by Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) and RT-qPCR. MGO increased nucleus-to-cytoplasm area ratio by 49% and dysregulated glucose handling, increasing 2-(N-(7-Nitrobenz-2-oxa-1,3-diazol-4-yl)Amino)-2-Deoxyglucose (2-NBDG) uptake by ~ 25%, with GLUT1/GLUT4 membrane redistribution; MNP-021 normalized morphology, glucose uptake, and transporter localization without cytotoxicity up to 10 µM. RNA-seq identified 754 MGO-deregulated genes, including ISR/metabolic nodes such as glucokinase (GCK), Sestrin-2 (SESN2), phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH), Phosphoserine Aminotransferase 1 (PSAT1), phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 2 (PCK2); MNP-021 buffered stress-induced transcription with limited baseline effects, modulated mitochondrial morphology and redox-associated fluorescence while preserving overall respiratory flux and blunting stress-evoked compensatory glycolysis. MNP-021 restored pro-survival signaling (pAKT/pERK and nuclear pCREB), including insulin responsiveness during MGO exposure. In a sustained high-glucose model, MNP-021 reduced the high-glucose-associated increase in cell death, extending its protective effects beyond the acute MGO paradigm. MNP-021 reduced Interleukine-6 (IL-6)/TNF-α release while increasing Interleukine-10 (IL-10) and Arginase 1 (ARG1) (~ 1.9-fold vs. LPS/TNF-α) in HMC3 glial cells, shifting them toward a pro-resolving IL-10/ARG1 program with reduced amyloid β-peptide 25-35 (Aβ(25-35))-evoked cytokine release and Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) remaining very low (≤ 10 pg/mL) and not significantly increased in this system. MNP-021 coordinates transcriptomic restraint, transporter-level glucose handling, mitochondrial resilience, and pro-survival/pro-resolving signaling in neuron-microglia cell models. These findings support further preclinical evaluation of MNP-021 in dicarbonyl-linked neuro-metabolic stress and provide pharmacological evidence consistent with a TRPA1-linked component of its activity.

title: RAMP3 is associated with macrophage-driven immune exclusion and promotes resistance to PD-1 blockade in breast cancer: integrated in vivo and single-cell transcriptomic analyses.
abstract: Receptor activity-modifying protein 3 (RAMP3) has been implicated in stromal regulation in cancer. However, its role in tumor microenvironment (TME) remodeling and immune checkpoint resistance remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to define the role of RAMP3 in shaping the immunosuppressive TME and evaluate its potential as a therapeutic target to enhance immunotherapy responses. We used syngeneic mouse models of breast cancer with genetic manipulation of RAMP3 to investigate tumor progression, immune remodeling, and response to immune checkpoint blockade in vivo. Tumor growth, metastasis, and survival were evaluated. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on murine tumor tissues, and a publicly available spatial transcriptomic dataset was analyzed to characterize immune cell states and spatial organization within the TME. Human breast cancer datasets from The Cancer Genome Atlas were analyzed to assess the clinical relevance of RAMP3-associated immune signatures. Our results suggest that RAMP3 contributed to the establishment of an immunosuppressive TME. In mouse models, RAMP3 deletion suppressed primary tumor growth, reduced lung metastasis, and improved survival. These effects were associated with a shift from M2-like tumor-associated macrophages to antigen-presenting macrophage states, increased CD8+ T cell infiltration, and reduced T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, RAMP3 deficiency was associated with reduced IL-4/STAT6 signaling in macrophages and decreased expression of immunosuppressive genes, including the chemokine CCL8. Pharmacological inhibition of CCL synthesis phenocopied the effects of RAMP3 deficiency, and RAMP3 deficiency enhanced the efficacy of PD-1 blockade. Spatial transcriptomic analysis demonstrated co-localization of RAMP3 and CCL8 within the TME. In the TCGA-BRCA cohort, a higher weighted RAMP3/CD163/CD8A risk score was associated with poorer overall survival and remained significantly associated with overall survival in complete-case multivariable Cox models adjusted for clinicopathological variables. RAMP3 was identified as a potential regulator of the immunosuppressive TME and its functional impact was demonstrated in vivo. Integration with human clinical datasets supports further investigation of RAMP3 as a potential therapeutic target for overcoming resistance to immune checkpoint therapy in breast cancer.

title: Donor-aware single-cell and cross-modal prioritization of candidate mesenchymal stromal cell extracellular-vesicle cargo-receptor contexts in human meniscus degeneration.
abstract: Computational mapping of extracellular-vesicle cargo to recipient-cell receptors can prioritize experiments, but donor non-independence, database bias, transcript thresholds, and clinical confounding can inflate inference. We developed a donor-aware cross-modal workflow and applied it to 14 human meniscus single-cell RNA-sequencing libraries from 13 donors (GSE220243). Donor-by-state pseudobulk models were combined with directional, full-subunit OmniPath verification, human mesenchymal stromal cell extracellular-vesicle (MSC-EV) protein evidence from ExoCarta, continuous receptor-complex bottleneck scores, 15 threshold-prevalence settings, 1000 stratified donor bootstraps, and 5000 expression- and ligand-degree-matched permutations. External evidence comprised PRJCA008120 marker sets, covariate-adjusted GSE98918 transcriptomics, and published PXD042122 proteomics. Quality control retained 86,953 singlets; after excluding one uncertain cluster, 17 annotated states remained, of which 13 were donor-eligible. Evidence gating reduced 69 legacy hypotheses to 38 cargo-receptor-pathway combinations involving eight ExoCarta-retained candidate cargos. No receptor-panel enrichment survived multiplicity correction in the matched-null audit. Relative to the reference setting, 194 of 195 state-setting comparisons retained identical top-10 receptor sets, and 96 of 442 receptor-state contexts remained top-10 in every bootstrap. In GSE98918, 1995 genes were significant before covariate adjustment, whereas none reached transcriptome-wide false-discovery-rate significance after adjustment. Four prespecified receptor components were quantified in PXD042122; ITGAV was lower in end-stage osteoarthritis medial meniscus (published q = 0.045). This workflow yields a reproducible, evidence-bounded shortlist of transcript-defined receptor contexts. It does not establish EV delivery, receptor activation, age-independent disease effects, or therapeutic efficacy.

title: Multi-dimensional structure and subtype-specific heterogeneity of angiogenesis in breast cancer.
abstract: The prognostic relevance of angiogenesis in breast cancer remains unclear when modeled as a coordinated gene program rather than individual gene effects. This study aimed to characterize the multidimensional structure of angiogenesis and assess the prognostic relevance of its latent components for overall survival in breast cancer. Using RNA sequencing data from 1,096 patients with The Cancer Genome Atlas Breast Invasive Carcinoma (TCGA-BRCA) from the United States, we summarized 36 angiogenesis-related genes via principal component analysis (PCA) applied to standardized log-counts per million values. The first three components ([Formula: see text]), retained based on variance explained, scree plot inspection, and interpretable gene loading patterns, were evaluated for association with overall survival using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age and molecular subtype. The first three components captured a multi-dimensional structure of angiogenesis activity. None was significantly associated with overall survival in multivariable Cox models (Z1: HR = 1.016, 95% CI: 0.957-1.078, p = 0.603; Z2: HR = 1.049, 95% CI: 0.954-1.153, p = 0.319; Z3: HR = 1.007, 95% CI: 0.918-1.105, p = 0.878), and Kaplan-Meier analyses showed no significant survival differences across median-based groups. Functional enrichment analyses indicated that the retained components represented distinct biological dimensions of angiogenesis. Subtype-specific analyses showed no statistically significant associations within individual subtypes and no strong evidence of effect modification. However, marked differences in latent component distributions across molecular subtypes revealed substantial subtype-specific heterogeneity. Collectively, these findings indicate limited independent prognostic relevance for overall survival despite substantial biological heterogeneity and subtype-specific variation. Angiogenesis is a multi-dimensional and biologically heterogeneous process. No latent angiogenesis component demonstrated independent prognostic value for overall survival, indicating that angiogenesis is insufficient as a standalone prognostic biomarker. Nevertheless, subtype-specific variation across latent dimensions highlights its relevance for understanding biological heterogeneity in breast cancer.

title: VAMP5 Mediates Sevoflurane-Induced Immune Modulation in Cervical Cancer: A Clinical Translational Study.
abstract: Sevoflurane, a commonly used inhaled anesthetic, has been implicated in modulating tumor biology and perioperative immune responses, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aims to investigate whether sevoflurane regulates key immune-related genes in cervical cancer patients undergoing laparoscopic radical hysterectomy (LRH) and to explore the clinical relevance of such regulation. Based on prior RNA-seq screening, we established a two-step validation framework to identify sevoflurane-regulated genes in a clinical cohort. A total of 116 cervical cancer patients undergoing LRH were enrolled, including 70 who received sevoflurane anesthesia and 46 who received propofol anesthesia. Peripheral blood samples were collected at five perioperative time points. mRNA expression levels of candidate genes were measured by qRT-PCR, lymphocyte subsets were analyzed by flow cytometry, and VAMP5 protein expression was assessed by intracellular staining. Bioinformatics analyses were performed using TCGA data to evaluate associations between candidate genes and tumor immune infiltration. MAP3K7 and VAMP5 were validated as sevoflurane-downregulated targets, showing sustained suppression postoperatively compared to the propofol group. VAMP5 expression correlated significantly with tumor progression and immune cell infiltration in cervical cancer, particularly CD8+ T-cells, B-cells, and macrophages. Among sevoflurane-treated patients, those with lower VAMP5 expression exhibited delayed postoperative recovery of CD8+ T-cell counts at 48 and 72 h after surgery, whereas no such difference was observed for other lymphocyte subsets. This study identify VAMP5 as a novel molecular link between anesthetic choice and immune modulation, suggesting that sevoflurane may influence perioperative immune recovery through vesicle-associated mechanisms, with potential implications for optimizing anesthesia strategies to improve oncologic outcomes.

title: Genotype-specific molecular and functional trajectories in NGLY1 deficiency: a comparative multi-omics study of patient-derived iPSC neurons.
abstract: NGLY1 deficiency is an ultra-rare congenital disorder of deglycosylation with prominent neurodevelopmental impairment and marked allelic heterogeneity. Prior human neuronal models have characterized NGLY1 loss largely within single genetic backgrounds, leaving open whether distinct patient genotypes converge on a shared molecular state or follow divergent routes. Because clinical presentations overlap across genotypes, resolving this question requires a direct, within-system comparison of multiple genotypes rather than characterization of any single line. We generated iPSC-derived glutamatergic neurons from three patients carrying distinct biallelic NGLY1 genotypes (R401X/R401X, Q208X/G310G, L318P/R390P) and two healthy controls, and profiled them head-to-head using matched transcriptomics and proteomics at day 28, RNA to protein concordance and differential exon usage analysis, pathway and phenotype network integration, and longitudinal multielectrode array (MEA) recordings during early network maturation. Across both molecular layers, samples segregated strongly by genotype rather than forming a unified disease signature. Differential expression revealed pronounced between-genotype heterogeneity with only a small shared molecular core. RNA to protein concordance was moderate and genotype-dependent, and differential exon usage was enriched among discordant genes in a mutation-dependent manner, implicating splicing-level regulation in the transcript to protein divergence. Integrated networks linked genotype-specific concordant changes to synaptic signaling, calcium handling, metabolism, and extracellular matrix remodeling, and connected them to overlapping clinical phenotypes through distinct molecular routes. MEA recordings showed delayed maturation and genotype-dependent shifts in network excitability, with functional clustering that mirrored the molecular separation. Distinct NGLY1 genotypes produce divergent molecular and functional trajectories that converge on impaired network maturation through non-identical routes. These findings reframe NGLY1 deficiency as a set of genotype-specific molecular states rather than a single phenotype, with direct implications for mechanistic subgrouping and the design of preclinical models and validation studies.

title: ADAM19 Promotes EMT-Related Changes and Serves as a Prognostic Marker in Circulating Tumor Cells of Renal Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Detection of circulating tumor cells (CTCs), particularly characterization of their epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) phenotypes, may improve prognostic accuracy for malignancies. Identification of novel biomarkers for CTC classification may improve the characterization of tumor progression and provide potential therapeutic insights for renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Herein, we identified that a disintegrin and metalloproteinase domain-containing protein 19 (ADAM19) was associated with EMT phenotypes of CTCs. In vitro functional experiments, Western blotting, and RNA sequencing demonstrated that ADAM19 promoted RCC malignant progression and EMT-related changes and was associated with NOTCH and NF-κB signaling pathways. Our findings further suggested potential bidirectional association between ADAM19 and these signaling pathways. CTCs isolated from xenograft mouse models exhibited enhanced proliferative, migratory, and invasive abilities, accompanied by increased ADAM19 expression compared with parental tumor cells. Clinical CTC analysis further revealed that ADAM19-Low-CTCs were associated with unfavorable clinical outcomes in RCC patients. Notably, higher time-updated ADAM19-Low-CTC counts were identified as an independent risk factor for progression-free survival (HR = 1.243, 95% CI: 1.006-1.536).

title: Insights into early-onset colorectal cancer from a single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas of colorectal cancer across the age continuum.
abstract: The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EO-CRC; diagnosed before age 50 years) is increasing worldwide. Although current data indicate that EO-CRC may be biologically distinct from average-onset CRC (AO-CRC; diagnosed at age ≥50 years), molecular differences remain poorly defined. To address this knowledge gap, we generated a single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) atlas from 189 primary CRC tumors (54 EO-CRC, 135 AO-CRC) spanning eight decades of life, with at least 20 tumors in most age decades. Our analyses stratified tumors by microsatellite status and accounted for tumor sidedness, stage, patient sex and neoadjuvant treatment history, modeling age continuously or categorically (EO-CRC versus AO-CRC). Among microsatellite-stable (MSS) tumors, those from younger patients were characterized by increased stromal and decreased epithelial proportions, which we confirmed using multispectral immunofluorescence and machine learning in an external cohort of 712 MSS CRC tumors (18 EO-CRC, 694 AO-CRC). Tumor epithelial cells from young patients exhibited increased expression of long noncoding RNAs and FN1, with a trend toward increased heterogeneity in copy number alterations. MSS left-sided EO-CRC tumors had more cell-cell interactions, with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition-related signaling pathways (FN1/GDF/ACTIVIN) showing increased, cell type-specific interactions. Our large high-resolution snRNA-seq atlas uncovers age-associated features of CRC and provides a resource for the community to understand EO-CRC biology.

title: N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Hepatic Angiotensinogen in Hypertension: A Phase I Clinical Trial With Randomized Part A and Open-Label Part B.
abstract: Angiotensinogen (AGT) is the precursor of angiotensin peptides and a key determinant of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system activity. ART101 is an investigational N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA (GalNAc-siRNA) designed to durably suppress hepatic AGT synthesis. To evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of single ascending doses of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA in healthy volunteers and to provide an initial exploratory assessment of blood pressure effects in patients with hypertension. This phase I study was conducted from January 2025 to April 2026 with 24-week follow-up. Part A was a double-blind, placebo-controlled, single ascending-dose trial; part B was an open-label, single-dose study. The study took place at Beijing Friendship Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, China. Part A enrolled 40 healthy adults randomized 6:2 to receive the GalNAc-siRNA (25-600 mg) or placebo; 39 completed the study. Part B enrolled 8 patients with hypertension receiving the GalNAc-siRNA, 600 mg; all completed the study. A single subcutaneous injection of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA (25, 75, 150, 300, or 600 mg) or placebo in part A; a single open-label subcutaneous injection of GalNAc-siRNA, 600 mg, in part B. The primary outcome was safety and tolerability; secondary outcomes included pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, exploratory blood pressure assessments, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system biomarkers. Among 40 healthy volunteers (27 [67.5%] male; mean [SD] age, 40.4 [7.8] years) and 8 patients (6 [75.0%] male; mean [SD] age, 47.3 [10.3] years) with hypertension, the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA was well tolerated. In part A, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) occurred in 23 of 30 active-treatment participants (76.7%) vs 7 of 10 placebo recipients (70.0%); in part B, 6 of 8 patients (75.0%) had TEAEs. No serious adverse events, injection site reactions, or hyperkalemia were observed; all TEAEs were mild to moderate. Plasma exposure (maximum plasma concentration [Cmax] and area under the plasma concentration-time curve [AUC]) increased with dose over the wide dose range from 25 mg to 600 mg. Mean maximum serum AGT reductions of 93% (at 600 mg) in healthy volunteers and 90% (at 600 mg) in patients with hypertension were observed. At 24 weeks after a single 600-mg dose, the placebo-corrected 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure decreased by 12.9 mm Hg in healthy participants. In this phase I study, no serious treatment-related safety signals were identified. Sustained, dose-dependent AGT reductions and exploratory blood pressure lowering were observed. These findings support further investigation of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA as a potential long-acting therapeutic for hypertension. China Drug Clinical Registry Identifiers: CTR20250041 (part A) and CTR20253973 (part B).

title: Atherosclerosis: From Pathogenesis to Therapeutic Interventions.
abstract: Atherosclerosis is no longer viewed solely as a lipid-storage disorder but rather as a complex multisystem inflammatory disease driven by interactions among the vascular, immune, metabolic, and nervous systems. This review integrates recent concepts, including trained immunity, the neuroimmune cardiovascular interface, vascular cell plasticity, and the microbiome-vascular axis, that reshape the understanding of plaque initiation, progression, and instability. We summarize how established lipid-lowering, antidiabetic, antihypertensive, and revascularization strategies influence atherosclerotic disease and discuss emerging interventions, including RNA therapeutics, anti-inflammatory agents, gene therapy, and cell-based approaches. Key ongoing clinical trials that may clarify the cardiovascular benefits and safety of these strategies are also reviewed. Despite therapeutic advances, residual cardiovascular risk persists because of limitations in animal models, sex-related differences in plaque phenotype, and the lack of clinically applicable biomarkers. Nanotechnology, human microphysiological systems, spatial multiomics, and artificial intelligence may help bridge these translational gaps. Successful clinical implementation will nevertheless require biomarker-guided patient selection, rational combination therapy, validated surrogate endpoints, long-term safety assessment, and attention to health economics. In summary, these advances will shape future translational research and clinical trial design, ultimately advancing personalized management of atherosclerosis.

title: Association of MAGEA4 expression with molecular and immune subtypes and clinical outcomes in recurrent bladder cancer.
abstract: This study assessed MAGEA4 expression in recurrent bladder cancer, examined its relationships with molecular and immune subtypes, and evaluated its association with treatment response and prognosis. This single-center exploratory cohort study enrolled 20 patients. RNA sequencing was performed on recurrent tumor tissue samples. The EU molecular subtypes were determined. Immune subtypes were classified, and PD-L1 and HER2 status were assessed. GO, KEGG, and Reactome enrichment analyses were performed. Patients were divided into MAGEA4-high and MAGEA4-low groups using the cohort median expression level. Differences in the composition of molecular/immune subtypes were compared. Within-cohort ROC analysis was used to assess discrimination of clinical benefit, and PFS was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox methods. The top 20 genes with the most prominent between-subtype expression differences were identified. Genes upregulated in the Luminal papillary subtype were enriched in terms related to cell-cell junctions and epithelial structure maintenance. Downregulated genes were enriched in pathways associated with immune activation and inflammatory infiltration. Enrichment signals involved the PI3K-Akt, MAPK, neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction, and JAK-STAT pathways. Significant differences in PD-L1 status, TMIT subtypes, and EU subtypes were observed between MAGEA4-high and MAGEA4-low groups, and the six MAGEA4-immune/molecular association tests remained below q<0.05 after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. MAGEA4 expression also differed according to PD-L1 status, TMIT subtype, and binary EU subtype grouping. Within-cohort ROC analysis yielded AUC values of 0.798, 0.800, and 0.750 in the overall, immunotherapy, and combination-therapy cohorts, respectively; the bootstrap optimism-corrected overall AUC was 0.793. High MAGEA4 expression was associated with shorter PFS. MAGEA4 expression was associated with PD-L1 status, TMIT immune subtypes, and EU molecular subtypes, showed within-cohort discrimination of clinical benefit, and was associated with poorer PFS. These findings support further evaluation of MAGEA4 as a candidate molecular stratification marker in independent cohorts.

title: Schisandrin B attenuates ischemic acute kidney injury in a CTR1-dependent manner by inhibiting cuproptosis.
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) remains a global health challenge with high mortality rates and no targeted pharmacotherapy. Although regulated cell death (RCD) drives renal tubular epithelial cell (RTEC) injury, the involvement of cuproptosis, a copper-triggered RCD characterized by lipoylated protein aggregation and iron-sulfur cluster loss, remains unexplored in acute kidney injury (AKI). Integrated single-cell transcriptomics (GSE180420), a human renal biopsy cohort (n = 22), ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) mouse models, and hypoxia-reoxygenation (H/R) cellular models were used to characterize cuproptosis. Multi-omics profiling, molecular docking, and CTR1 (encoded by SLC31A1)-specific siRNA knockdown were used to explore the mechanism of action of Schisandrin B (SchB). Single-cell RNA sequencing of murine ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) kidneys revealed that cuproptosis was a predominant RCD modality, accounting for approximately one-third of all regulated cell death events in renal tubular epithelial cells (RTECs). This finding was corroborated in human AKI biopsies and in murine I/R kidneys, where the key cuproptosis proteins ferredoxin 1 (FDX1) and copper transporter 1 (CTR1) were markedly upregulated, accompanied by significant copper accumulation and tubule injury. Under the tested conditions, SchB exhibited protective effects at least comparable to those of the classical copper chelator tetrathiomolybdate (TTM) in attenuating copper-dependent cytotoxicity in vitro. SchB-regulated differentially expressed genes were significantly enriched in glutathione metabolism, p53 signaling, cellular senescence, and PI3K-Akt pathways. Molecular docking predicted a direct interaction between SchB and CTR1 (binding energy -5.1 kcal/mol)siRNA-mediated depletion of CTR1 partially abolished the protective effects of SchB against copper-induced RTEC death, indicating that CTR1 may be required, at least in part, for SchB-induced cytoprotection in RTECs. This study identifies cuproptosis as a predominant and previously unrecognized RCD pathway in ischemic AKI. SchB inhibits cuproptosis in a CTR1-dependent manner. These findings provide a preclinical rationale for further investigation of this natural product as a potential therapeutic candidate for ischemic kidney disease.

title: Identification of glutathione metabolism-related biomarkers in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease based on single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing.
abstract: Glutathione (GSH) metabolism plays a crucial role in the development and progression of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), yet its molecular mechanism remains unclear. Bulk transcriptome and single-cell data from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database were analyzed using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and five algorithms for Glutathione metabolism-related genes (GMRGs) scores to identify key cell types and biomarkers. Core candidate biomarker was validated by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and western blotting in palmitic acid (PA)-induced HepG2 cells. Cholangiocytes showed the highest GMRG-related transcriptional activity among the annotated cell populations. Through screening, 4 potential biomarkers (CSTA, DDAH2, OAZ2, TYMP) were found, with DDAH2 as the core due to its high expression and strong correlation with GMRGs. Enrichment analysis suggested that DDAH2 expression was associated with energy metabolism and protein homeostasis pathways. DDAH2-high cholangiocytes showed stronger computationally inferred interactions with B cells and endothelial cells, mainly involving the "MIF-(CD74 + CXCR4)" and "APP-CD74" pathways, and were enriched in early pseudotime states. In vitro, DDAH2 expression was significantly up-regulated in NAFLD, providing preliminary support for the expression trend. This study identified cholangiocytes as the annotated cell population with the strongest GSH metabolism-related transcriptional signature in the analyzed NAFLD scRNA-seq dataset and highlighted four related biomarkers, with DDAH2 prioritized as the core candidate biomarker.

title: Decoder-FFPE-seq enables sensitive, genome-wide spatial transcriptomics of archival tissues at single-cell resolution.
abstract: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue-compatible spatial transcriptomics (ST) is transforming biology and histopathology, but achieving high sensitivity, genome-wide coverage, single-cell resolution, and researcher accessibility remains challenging. To address these challenges, we here present a dendrimeric DNA coordinate barcoding design for FFPE tissue-adapted spatial RNA sequencing (Decoder-FFPE-seq) by integrating RNA-to-DNA probe conversion with blotting-assisted barcoding. Decoder-FFPE-seq provides single-cell resolution with a >2.6-fold sensitivity increase in whole-transcriptome mouse brain and archived human sample profiling over existing platforms, resolving potential cellular identity of low-abundance genes, finer tissue architecture, and capturing an epithelial-mesenchymal transition-associated signature for prognostic value. With expanded probe libraries, Decoder-FFPE-seq captures long noncoding and viral RNAs, revealing their spatial coregulatory networks with messenger RNAs in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCCs). In an OSCC immunotherapy cohort, two CD8+ T cell subpopulations were respectively identified in pre- and postchemoimmunotherapy samples, potentially linked to treatment response. Decoder-FFPE-seq establishes a robust, high-resolution, and accessible framework for sensitive ST profiling of archival tissues in fundamental and translational studies.

title: Epigenetic silencing of PDLIM4 promotes colorectal cancer by impairing BTF3 autophagic degradation and activating PI3K/Akt signalling.
abstract: Epigenetic silencing of tumour suppressor genes is a pivotal early event in colorectal cancer (CRC) pathogenesis. PDZ and LIM Domain 4 (PDLIM4) is a member of the PDZ-LIM family with context-dependent roles in tumour progression across different malignancies. However, its specific role and epigenetic regulation in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain elusive. We integrated multi-omics datasets and clinical cohorts to evaluate PDLIM4 expression and promoter methylation. Stool DNA was analyzed to assess the feasibility of non-invasive detection of PDLIM4 promoter methylation. PDLIM4 knockout and overexpression cell lines were constructed to perform functional assays including proliferation, apoptosis, and stemness. In vivo experiments were validated utilizing xenograft mice or an azoxymethane (AOM)/ dextran sulphate sodium salt (DSS) CRC mouse model with intestinal epithelial cell-specific overexpression of PDLIM4. Mechanistic investigations were conducted using coimmunoprecipitation coupled with mass spectrometry, RNA sequencing, ChIP-qPCR and pharmacological rescue experiments. We identified a progressive loss of PDLIM4 protein along the normal-adenoma-carcinoma sequence, driven by DNMT3A-mediated promoter hypermethylation, and lower PDLIM4 expression was associated with adverse patient prognosis. PDLIM4 methylation was also significantly increased in stool DNA from CRC patients compared with healthy controls. Mechanistically, genetic ablation of PDLIM4 significantly blunted the therapeutic efficacy of the DNA demethylating agent 5-Azacytidine against CRC. Functionally, PDLIM4 restoration suppressed CRC cell proliferation and stemness while enhancing apoptosis in vitro, and reduced tumour growth in both AOM/DSS and xenograft models in vivo. At the molecular level, PDLIM4 interacted with BTF3 and promoted its autophagic-lysosomal degradation, thereby limiting PI3K/Akt signalling, with NTRK2 identified as a potential transcriptional target linking BTF3 to PI3K/Akt activation. DNMT3A-mediated silencing of PDLIM4 is an early epigenetic event that facilitates CRC progression. PDLIM4 suppresses tumour growth by promoting BTF3 degradation, thereby restricting PI3K/Akt signalling. Thus, PDLIM4 methylation may have potential as a biomarker for early CRC detection. DNMT3A-mediated PDLIM4 promoter hypermethylation is an early event in colorectal tumorigenesis. Restoring PDLIM4 suppresses CRC proliferation and stemness while promoting apoptosis in vitro and in vivo. PDLIM4 promotes the autophagic-lysosomal degradation of BTF3 and restrains PI3K/Akt signalling. Stool DNA analysis supports the potential of PDLIM4 methylation as a non-invasive CRC biomarker.
